chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"Shortening [the prayer] is [permitted] when traveling a farasikh, and a farasikh is four farsakhs."

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: Shortening of the four-rak'ah prayer during travel
key_terms.بَرِيد: A unit of distance, often referring to a farasikh or a specific travel distance
key_terms.فَرَاسِخَ: Plural of farasikh, a traditional unit of distance

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum distance for shortening prayers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the specific distance of four farsakhs as the threshold for the obligation of shortening prayers (qasr) during travel. In Shia jurisprudence, this narration is pivotal for defining the 'qasr' condition, distinguishing it from the 'jam'' (combining) rules which may apply at shorter distances, and reflects the practical application of the Prophet's tradition on the road. The measurement of four farsakhs serves as a foundational metric in the Usuli school for determining when a traveler's status changes, impacting both prayer and other legal rulings.
